multi-select.purpose: Select multiple fleets, vehicles, regions, tags, permissions, or owners with clear count, removal, bulk behavior, validation, and recovery.
useWhen: Users need to choose more than one item from a known set.
Selection count, removable chips, or apply/cancel behavior matters.
Choices affect filtering, permissions, notifications, or ownership.
doNotUseWithoutReview: Only one value can be selected.
The selection set is too large without search or grouping.
Apply behavior, persistence, or max count is unclear.
foundations: Defines list density, chip wrapping, apply bar, and responsive stacking.
Owns labels, count copy, max selection copy, and empty recovery.
Controls selected, disabled, warning, and focus states.
Empty, partial, all selected, over limit, disabled, dirty, and applied states are explicit.
Selection updates are stable and avoid layout jumps.
Requires checkbox semantics, count text, keyboard access, and removable selection names.
slots: Opens selection surface when not inline.
Selectable items with labels and optional descriptions.
Commits dirty selection when explicit apply is required.
Explains required, max, or unavailable selection.
variants: Checkbox list with selected chips and apply action.
Validation appears when the max count is exceeded.
Empty State or helper copy explains recovery.
motion: Count and chips update without moving focus.
Max selection warning appears inline without overlay.
accessibility: Remove controls include selected item names.
Validation is associated with the group.
Keyboard users can select, remove, and apply.
tests: Selecting options updates count and chips.
Removing a chip unchecks the option.
Clearing all selections shows empty recovery.

canDecide: Use Multi Select when users need more than one value.
Use chips when selected values need review or removal.
Use explicit apply when selection affects a costly query.
mustAsk: Max count, persistence, permission scope, or apply behavior is unclear.
rejectIf: Only one value can be selected.
Selected items cannot be reviewed or removed.
miel.handoff: Confirm selection source, max count, apply behavior, persistence, empty state, and validation.
